questions.q_en:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Being an oldest member of the club, / he was often consulted by others / for his valuable advice and experience.
options_en: for his valuable advice and experience
Being an oldest member of the club,
he was often consulted by others
questions.solution_en:
The error is in the part "Being an oldest member of the club,". "Oldest" is a superlative adjective. Superlative adjectives are usually preceded by the definite article "the" because they indicate a unique item or person in a group. "An" (indefinite article) is incorrect here.

Correct Sentence: Being the oldest member of the club, he was often consulted by others for his valuable advice and experience.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

Note:

· Definite and indefinite articles: In the English language, we have one definite article 'the'; it refers to or introduces, a particular, specific noun. 'An' and 'a' are indefinite articles. Superlative adjectives (like "oldest") generally require the definite article "the."

· The Superlative degree: Indicates the highest degree of quality and is used when more than two things (or sets of things) are compared.

questions.q_en:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A) Addressing child labour requires stringent laws, enforcement, and global cooperation to ensure children are protected and educated.

B) Many children are subjected to long hours and dangerous conditions, impacting their physical and mental health.

C) Child labour deprives children of their childhood, education, and potential, forcing them into hazardous work environments.

D) By eliminating child labour, we pave the way for a future where every child can thrive and contribute positively to society.
questions.solution_en:
If the sentences are read carefully, it can be noted that sentences C and B talk about the central idea of the passage which is 'child labour' and its explanation. So, they have to come first so that the rest of the sentences can be arranged accordingly. Sentence A offers a suggestion that can be the solution to child labour so it can follow the pair and sentence D concludes the passage by describing the aftermath of eliminating child labour. So, the final order of the sentences is CBAD.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.q_en:
In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option.

He said to me that he was focusing (A)/ on batting even though (B)/ his bowling figures have not been (C)/ impressive in the ongoing tournament. (D)
questions.solution_en:
Part A has an error.

When used with a that-clause, 'tell' takes an indirect object, while 'say' does not.

Example sentence: Ramya told me (that) she would arrive early today. (not: told (that))

Ramya said (that) she would arrive early today. (not: said to me)

Therefore, in the given sentence, the phrase 'said to me' is incorrect.

The correct sentence is: He told me that he was focusing on batting even though his bowling figures have not been impressive in the ongoing tournament.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

questions.solution_en:
The sentence in the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense.

There are three cases when the Indirect Speech is in Past Perfect Tense.

· Tense remains same

· Past perfect changes to Present Perfect

· Past perfect changes to Simple Past

Case 1: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object) tense will be kept intact.

For example:

He said that he had just finished the movie. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I had just finished the movie" (Direct Speech)

Case 2: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 +Object) will be converted into Present Perfect (Subject + has/have + V3 +Object).

For example:

He said that he had got a new job. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "I have got a new job." (Direct Speech)

Case 3: Past Perfect (Subject + had + V3 + Object) will be converted into Past Simple (Subject + V2 + Object).

For example:

He said that Arya had sent him a book. (Indirect Speech)

He said, "Arya sent me a book" (Direct Speech)

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

Here, "had been" changes to "has been".

Here, the use of "informs" in option 4 is incorrect as reporting verb should be in past tense for a past tense sentence.

So, option 1 is correct here.

options_en: I have been working from home since last year.
I have been working from home from last year.
I have been working from home for last year.
I have been working from home to last year.
questions.solution_en:

From and since indicate a point of time while for indicates a period of time.

'To' is used to indicate a range or period of time.

Examples: The show will run from 10 a.m. to 2 p.m. She has not spoken to him since last year. I have not met her for 10 years now. It takes five to ten minutes to finish

So, as per the rule, the correct sentence is - I have been working from home since last year.

Hence, option (a) is correct.

questions.q_en:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

P. a vast majority of flowering plants

Q. to agricultural biodiversity and food security,

R. as these insects are crucial pollinators for

S. the decline of global bee populations poses a significant threat
questions.solution_en:
The sentence logically begins with part S, "The decline of global bee populations poses a significant threat," which introduces the main subject "The decline of global bee populations" and its primary action "poses a significant threat."

Part Q, "to agricultural biodiversity and food security," directly follows S, specifying what the "significant threat" (mentioned in S) is directed towards, using the preposition "to."

Next, part R, "as these insects are crucial pollinators for," provides the reason or explanation for the threat mentioned. The conjunction "as" introduces this causal clause, and "these insects" refers back to the "bee populations" from part S.

Finally, part P, "a vast majority of flowering plants," completes the clause started in R, specifying what the insects are pollinators for, thus concluding the sentence with the full impact of the bee population decline.

Thus, the correct and meaningful order of the sentence is SQRP.

The complete sentence after rearrangement is: The decline of global bee populations poses a significant threat to agricultural biodiversity and food security, as these insects are crucial pollinators for a vast majority of flowering plants.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

Option (a) uses the future tense ("will get"), which suggests that the action of sweeping the ball excellently will occur in the future. But the sentence describes a habitual or general action that Meenakshi performs when faced with an off-spin delivery. The simple present tense is more appropriate for expressing habitual actions or general truths.

Option (b) uses the present perfect tense ("has got"), which indicates an action that started in the past and has relevance to the present moment. The present perfect tense is not suitable in the given context because the sentence does not emphasise the completion of the action, but rather the habit of sweeping the ball excellently in response to an off-spin delivery.

Option (c) uses the simple past tense ("got"), which indicates an action that occurred in the past. But the sentence does not describe a specific past event. Accordingly, this option is incorrect. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

But they knew elephants, lions and other animals sometimes killed sleeping hunters. And there were some bad people, too, in the bush.

The hunters came to a place with big trees around it. They decided to rest and sleep on the grass. They did not make a fire and ate only some nuts which they carried in their bags. That was their supper. Then they went to sleep. All of them were tired. They slept soundly and did not hear anything. They did not hear that their enemies were coming nearer and nearer to them. But in one of the trees above the sleeping men, something moved and fell on the head of a young hunter. He jumped up and cried a big python was on his head!

The Naayire hunters got up quickly and saw the enemies around them. A fight began. Soon the enemies ran away and that was the end of the fight. The Naayire hunters came up to their chief to talk about the fight. "What made you jump up?" the chief asked the young hunter. "It was a python," he said. "It fell on my head, but it did not kill me." Then the chief said, "From this day on our people will never kill a python. That python saved our lives. Pythons will be sacred animals in our country." Even today the Naayire people love pythons. If you go into their houses in the rainy season, you will find a python there. The pythons never harm anyone. They don't eat even the chickens.

questions.solution_en:
'Sacred' means characterised by solemn religious ceremony or religious use. 'Profane' means ritually impure or unclean. So, the two words can be used as antonyms of each other. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

'Holy' means dedicated to a religious purpose.

'Pure' means free of flaws or imperfections.

'Protected' means guarded.

questions.q_en:
Identify the pair of synonyms from the underlined words in the given sentence.

The CEO's abrupt decision to terminate the project was an unexpected move that left the entire team feeling confused and disappointed, creating a sudden and significant shift in company morale.
questions.solution_en:
Option (a): "Abrupt" means sudden and unexpected. "Sudden" means occurring or done quickly and unexpectedly or without warning. These words are very close in meaning, making them synonyms.

Option (b): "Terminate" means to bring to an end. "Significant" means sufficiently great or important to be worthy of attention. They are unrelated in meaning.

Option (c): "Unexpected" means not expected or regarded as likely to happen. "Entire" means with no part left out; whole. These are not synonyms.

Option (d): "Confused" means unable to think clearly; bewildered. "Disappointed" means sad or displeased because someone or something has failed to fulfill one's hopes. They are different emotions.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.
